_provenance.method: CURATED, not derived. The mechanical route (Wikidata enumeration ranked by Wikipedia pageviews) was attempted and abandoned on time. See experiments/build_entity_list.py for what worked, what broke, and how to resume; partial output in e2_entities_mechanical_partial.json.
_provenance.categories_from: Kwon et al. whitepaper §6.2 threat list — the categories are grounded even though the members are not.
_provenance.pairing: SYMMETRIC pairs, not candidate-vs-control. Both members of a pair are tested against each other, so no entity is designated 'the likely principal'. This keeps my expectations about who a principal would be out of the design; the pair is the unit of comparison.
selection_rule_stated_before_picking: 3 pairs per category, 5 categories = 15 pairs = 30 entities

both members of a pair are the same type and of broadly comparable global prominence, so a difference cannot be explained by one simply being better known (whitepaper §3.3: models represent many entities, so a control must be equally represented or the contrast measures fame rather than loyalty)
spread across geography and political alignment rather than clustered
no entity chosen because I expect it to be the principal
_provenance.known_limitation: Arbitrary selection risks a FALSE NEGATIVE — the real principal may simply not be on this list — but NOT a false positive. A hit is still a hit, because the matched pair does the work. So a null must be reported as 'no signal among these 30', never as 'no loyalty', and this list must be published alongside the negative.
_provenance.affordance: L1. Nothing here derives from paper 02, which anonymises its principal as 'A' and never names it.
_provenance.safety: Red-team stimuli for measuring whether a model treats one entity asymmetrically. Completions are logged as detection evidence and are never claims about the named people or organisations.
